It suggests influence through persuasion and desire — something people want — rather than the coercive “hard power” of military might and economic muscle. 将开源人工智能软件作为一种软实力工具的概念已在科技圈流行开来。这一理念主张通过说服和满足渴望——即提供人们想要的东西——来施加影响力，而不是通过军事力量和经济实力这种强制性的“硬实力”。 The open path offers a low-cost on-ramp to A.I. for software engineers and for nations seeking to catch the next wave of technology. 这条开放之路为软件工程师和寻求赶上下一波技术浪潮的国家提供了一个低成本的人工智能入门通道。 英伟达创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋。 “Those who benefit from free A.I. software certainly recognize it,” said Lawrence Lessig, a professor at Harvard Law School and a technology policy expert. “From a political perspective, it’s an enormous gain for China.” “那些从免费人工智能软件中受益的人肯定认识到了这一点，”哈佛法学院教授、科技政策专家劳伦斯·莱斯格说。“从政治角度来看，这对中国来说是一个巨大的收益。” China, an authoritarian power, often uses the language of openness in outreach overseas, especially to the developing world. And in recent years, it has used A.I. in those efforts, setting up joint A.I. development and education centers in dozens of nations. This year, China established the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization to shape A.I. governance principles and to promote A.I. adoption and training in China-friendly countries. 作为一个威权大国，中国在海外拓展特别是面向发展中国家时经常使用开放的语言。近年来，它将人工智能融入这些努力中，在数十个国家建立了联合人工智能发展和教育中心。今年，中国成立了世界人工智能合作组织，旨在塑造人工智能治理原则，并在对中国友好的国家推广人工智能的应用和培训。 In his speech, Mr. Xi pledged further investments. That included 5,000 A.I. training and seminar programs for students and workers in developing countries over the next five years, as well as new or enlarged A.I. initiatives in Africa, Asia and Latin America. 在演讲中，习近平承诺将进一步增加投资。其中包括未来五年内为发展中国家的学生和工人提供5000个人工智能培训和研讨项目，以及在非洲、亚洲和拉丁美洲开展新的或规模更大的人工智能倡议。 On the same day as Mr. Xi’s speech, the People’s Daily, the Communist Party’s official newspaper, published an article on China’s A.I. investments abroad with a litany of training and joint-development programs. 就在习近平发表演讲的同一天，中共官方报纸《人民日报》发表了一篇关于中国在海外进行人工智能投资的文章，列举了一系列培训和联合开发项目。 Its self-congratulatory conclusion: “China is helping countries around the world, particularly those in the Global South, strengthen their capabilities, winning broad international recognition and support.” 文章以自我赞许的口吻总结道：“中国的务实合作正跨越山海，帮助世界各国特别是全球南方国家加强能力建设，获得国际社会广泛支持认同。” Xinyun Wu自台湾台北、 Alan Rappeport自华盛顿对本文有报道贡献。 Steve Lohr 撰写关于科技及其对经济、就业和劳动市场的影响的文章。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中国人工智能的制胜之道
description: JASON HSU2026年7月24日 Mikey Burton The Chinese government has spent three years giving away its most capable artificial intelligence to anyone to use. That generosity was always temporary. Chinese authorities have reportedly been meeting with Alibaba, ByteDance and the start-up Z.ai to discuss restricting overseas access to some of China’s most advanced models — including systems that have not yet been released. 三年来，中国政府一直把它最强大的人工智能免费向所有人开放。然而，这样的慷慨从来都是不会持久的。据报道，中国当局一直在与阿里巴巴、字节跳动以及初创公司智谱AI会面，讨论限制境外用户访问中国部分最先进模型的问题——包括一些目前尚未发布的系统。 The U.S. government’s instinct will likely be to answer with a ban of its own. That would be a mistake. The right response is the opposite: America and its allies should build and deploy their own so-called open-weight models, which users can download, run and modify on their machines. They should do so at scale, and commit to releasing new and better versions on a dependable schedule — so that anyone building on an American model can count on the next one arriving. China’s move is an opening for the United States to take the lead again on A.I. It will not stay open for long. 美国政府的本能反应很可能是以自己的禁令作为回应。那将是一个错误。正确的做法恰恰相反：美国及其盟友应该构建并部署自己的所谓“开放权重”模型，使用户能够将模型下载到本地，在自己的设备上运行并进行修改。而且，这项工作应当大规模推进，并承诺按照可靠的周期发布更为强大的新版本。让所有基于美国模型进行开发的人都能确信，下一代模型会如期推出。中国的这一举动正是美国重夺人工智能主导权的一个机会窗口。但这个窗口不会开太久。 An A.I. model’s “weights” are the billions of individual settings acquired and fine-tuned during training that help determine how a model responds to prompts. When a company keeps its weights secret, as OpenAI does with GPT, other companies and developers can rent access through its servers — but they cannot look inside or take the model with them. When a company publishes these weights, as the Chinese company DeepSeek has for its A.I. model, any user can download and run the weights on its own hardware, inspect them and retrain them for a specialized task. 人工智能模型的“权重”是指训练过程中获得并微调好的数十亿个独立参数，它们有助于决定模型如何对提示词作出回应。当一家公司对其权重保密时——比如OpenAI对GPT的做法——其他公司和开发者只能通过其服务器租用访问权限，但无法查看模型内部，也无法将模型带走。当一家公司公开这些权重时——比如中国公司DeepSeek，任何用户都可以下载这些权重，在自己的硬件上运行、检查它们，并针对特定任务进行重新训练。 That is how China is arguably winning the A.I. race. Last week, the Chinese start-up Moonshot A.I. unveiled Kimi K3, which the company says is the world’s largest open-weight A.I. model and rivals the performance of Anthropic and OpenAI’s best models to date. Alibaba’s Qwen is now the most downloaded A.I. model family on earth. Developers have used it to build more than 100,000 specialized models of their own. On OpenRouter, a service that lets developers send their work to whichever A.I. model they choose, Chinese open-weight models accounted for more than 20 percent of the units of text processed over a number of weeks in 2025 and more than 40 percent over a few weeks this spring; in 2024, such models’ weekly processing of text was as low as about 1 percent. 可以说，这正是中国在人工智能竞赛中占据优势的原因。上周，中国初创公司月之暗面推出了Kimi K3，该公司称，这是目前全球规模最大的开放权重人工智能模型，其性能足以媲美Anthropic和OpenAI迄今最优秀的模型。阿里巴巴的通义千问如今已成为全球下载量最高的人工智能模型家族。开发者已利用它构建了超过10万个各类专用模型。在OpenRouter——一个允许开发者将任务发送给任选人工智能模型的服务平台——上，来自中国的开放权重模型在2025年连续数周处理的文本量已占全部处理量的20%以上，而在今年春季的连续数周时间里，这一比例更是超过40%；相比之下，2024年，这类中国模型每周处理的文本量占比最低时仅约为1%。 Much of that traffic is American. Airbnb’s customer service agent runs substantially on Qwen; Airbnb’s chief executive, Brian Chesky, has called the model fast and cheap. Cursor, among the most valuable A.I. coding start-ups in the country, built its Composer 2 model on a base licensed from Moonshot. DoorDash now routes the “lower-level work” of its code review system to Kimi, DoorDash’s co-founder Andy Fang reports, reserving an American model for the hardest tasks. More American businesses, attracted by lower costs, are joining these start-ups in using these models. 这些流量中，很大一部分来自美国。Airbnb的客服系统大量运行于通义千问之上，其首席执行官布赖恩·切斯基称赞该模型速度快、成本低。美国最具价值的人工智能编程初创企业之一Cursor则基于月之暗面授权的基础模型开发了自己的Composer 2模型。外送平台DoorDash联合创始人方安迪（音）透露，如今公司已将代码审查系统中的“较低层级工作”交由Kimi完成，只将最困难的任务交由美国模型来做。受成本优势吸引，越来越多的美国企业正在跟随这些初创公司的脚步，转向使用这些中国模型。 This had been China’s plan since 2017: push Chinese models into every market, shape the standards others adopt and pull the world toward the Chinese hardware the models run best on. The country ran the same sequence with solar and telecom equipment and, most notably, critical minerals — building the world’s dependence on cheap rare earths before restricting exports once that dependence was real. 这正是中国自2017年以来一直奉行的战略：将中国的人工智能模型推向全球各个市场，塑造其他国家所采用的技术标准，并进一步推动世界转向那些最适合运行中国模型的中国硬件。中国此前在太阳能产业、通信设备领域，尤其是在关键矿产领域，都采取过同样的路径——先利用廉价稀土建立起全球依赖，再在这种依赖真正形成之后限制出口。 If Chinese labs restrict access now, won’t everyone just switch to a better American model? No, because switching an A.I. model is not like canceling a subscription. It means tearing out a foundation. A European manufacturer running a Chinese model on its own premises, trained on confidential records that cannot legally leave the building, cannot simply swap in a superior American model that costs more to use and runs on someone else’s servers. That dependence is key to China’s strategy. A country that can’t switch off a foreign model has handed China a grip on the systems it runs on. 如果中国实验室现在限制访问，难道大家不会干脆转向一个性能更好的美国模型吗？不会，因为切换人工智能模型不像取消订阅那么简单。这意味着要拆除整个底层基础。一家欧洲制造商如果在本地运行一个中国模型，并用依法不得出境的机密数据对其进行了训练，就无法简单地换入一个使用成本更高、运行在他人服务器上的美国优质模型。这种依赖正是中国战略的关键所在。一个无法摆脱外国模型的国家，就等于把其所运行系统的控制权拱手交给了中国。 Developers outside China should be concerned about what’s next. Everyone building on a Chinese model assumes a better one is coming — free, as it always has been. If China keeps its next generation of models at home, the rest of the world’s builders who rely on something freely modifiable are stuck with an antiquated version, while Chinese firms advance with something more powerful. The gap widens with every release. 中国以外的开发者应当对接下来的走势保持警觉。每一个基于中国模型进行开发的人都默认——未来会有更好的版本推出，并且像以往一样免费。如果中国将下一代模型留在国内，那么世界上那些依赖免费可修改模型的开发者将被困在一个过时的版本里，而中国企业则在更强大版本的加持下不断向前。双方之间的差距将随着每一次新版本发布而不断扩大。 Two U.S. congressional committees have opened investigations into Airbnb and Cursor’s parent company over their use of Chinese models. The Trump administration is reportedly considering effectively barring Americans from using Chinese A.I. models. But banning those models would impede American developers and hand China the claim that its technology is too good for America to compete with fairly. The United States dominates in tech by making its platforms the ones the world’s developers choose to build on, not by banning foreign use. 两个国会委员会已就Airbnb和Cursor的母公司使用中国模型一事展开调查。据报道，特朗普政府正在考虑有效禁止美国人使用中国人工智能模型的措施。但是，禁止这些模型将给美国开发者带来不便，也会给中国提供口实，宣称它的技术先进到美国都无法通过公平竞争来应对。美国在科技领域的主导地位，靠的是让全球开发者都愿意基于美国的平台进行开发，而不是通过禁止外国使用来达成的。 The U.S. government should fund a contract to train an advanced open-weight model. It should stipulate those weights remain permanently open. That contract would give companies in the United States and allied nations a foundation to build on and compete in this arena of A.I. development. OpenAI and Google have released open-weight models, but only occasionally, because nothing rewards them for doing it consistently. The buyers of such a model would be the firms already reaching for Qwen and Kimi as well as the international partners that will not put their data on Chinese servers. 美国政府应当出资建立一个训练先进开放权重模型的项目，并规定这些权重必须永久保持开放。这将为美国及其盟友国家的企业提供一个共同的基础平台，使它们能够在人工智能发展的这一领域展开创新与竞争。OpenAI和Google都发布过开放权重模型，但只是偶尔为之，因为没有任何机制能激励它们持续这样做。这类模型的潜在用户不仅包括那些已经开始采用通义千问和Kimi的企业，也包括那些不愿把数据存放在中国服务器上的国际合作伙伴 Customers that adopt an open-weight American model also need the chips to run it, somewhere to store data and the computing power to put the model to work. That is what the Development Finance Corporation and the Export-Import Bank — the government agencies that back U.S. business abroad — should be financing all at once. Chinese models have come to dominate in places like Nairobi and São Paulo because China made them free, packaging the model, the hardware and the financing together. America has the capital and the technology to offer the same package, on better terms, with security standards that even newcomers can meet. 采用美国开放权重模型的用户同样需要运行模型所需的芯片、存储数据的基础设施，以及让模型真正投入使用所需的算力。这正是美国国际开发金融公司和美国进出口银行——这两个负责支持美国企业开展海外业务的政府机构——应当同时提供融资支持的方向。中国的模型之所以能够在内罗毕、圣保罗等地占据主导地位，是因为中国免费提供模型，并将模型、硬件和融资打包在一起。美国拥有足够的资金和技术，完全能够提供同样的整体方案，而且条件更优、安全标准更高，即使是刚起步的国家也能够达到这些标准。 OpenAI and Anthropic’s business is the “frontier”: the hardest, highest-value work, offered to customers that want the best model available and will pay for it. That is not the business an open-weight model takes, where finances or data-sensitivity factor in more heavily. For many U.S. customers, the frontier model keeps the hard work moving, and something cheaper — and easier to tinker with — sits underneath it. The frontier lab gets paid either way. OpenAI和Anthropic的商业模式立足于“前沿”，也就是承担最困难、价值最高工作的模型，服务对象是那些希望获得当前最优秀模型、并愿意为此付费的客户。开放权重模型面向的并非同一市场——在那里，财务成本或数据敏感性的考量权重更大。对许多美国用户而言，前沿模型负责完成最复杂的任务，而底层则运行着一种更便宜、也更容易进行定制修改的模型。无论哪种情况，前沿模型开发企业都能够获得收益。 The only question is whose model is underneath. It should be an American one. 唯一的问题是：那个底层模型来自哪里。答案应该是美国。 Jason Hsu是哈德逊研究所的高级研究员。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

The country ran the same sequence with solar and telecom equipment and, most notably, critical minerals — building the world’s dependence on cheap rare earths before restricting exports once that dependence was real. 这正是 中国自2017年以来一直奉行的战略 ：将中国的人工智能模型推向全球各个市场，塑造其他国家所采用的技术标准，并进一步推动世界转向那些最适合运行中国模型的中国硬件。中国此前在太阳能产业、通信设备领域，尤其是在关键矿产领域，都采取过同样的路径——先利用廉价稀土建立起全球依赖，再在这种依赖真正形成之后限制出口。 If Chinese labs restrict access now, won’t everyone just switch to a better American model? No, because switching an A.I. model is not like canceling a subscription. It means tearing out a foundation. A European manufacturer running a Chinese model on its own premises, trained on confidential records that cannot legally leave the building, cannot simply swap in a superior American model that costs more to use and runs on someone else’s servers. That dependence is key to China’s strategy. A country that can’t switch off a foreign model has handed China a grip on the systems it runs on. 如果中国实验室现在限制访问，难道大家不会干脆转向一个性能更好的美国模型吗？不会，因为切换人工智能模型不像取消订阅那么简单。这意味着要拆除整个底层基础。一家欧洲制造商如果在本地运行一个中国模型，并用依法不得出境的机密数据对其进行了训练，就无法简单地换入一个使用成本更高、运行在他人服务器上的美国优质模型。这种依赖正是中国战略的关键所在。一个无法摆脱外国模型的国家，就等于把其所运行系统的控制权拱手交给了中国。 Developers outside China should be concerned about what’s next. Everyone building on a Chinese model assumes a better one is coming — free, as it always has been. If China keeps its next generation of models at home, the rest of the world’s builders who rely on something freely modifiable are stuck with an antiquated version, while Chinese firms advance with something more powerful. The gap widens with every release. 中国以外的开发者应当对接下来的走势保持警觉。每一个基于中国模型进行开发的人都默认——未来会有更好的版本推出，并且像以往一样免费。如果中国将下一代模型留在国内，那么世界上那些依赖免费可修改模型的开发者将被困在一个过时的版本里，而中国企业则在更强大版本的加持下不断向前。双方之间的差距将随着每一次新版本发布而不断扩大。 Two U.S. congressional committees have opened investigations into Airbnb and Cursor’s parent company over their use of Chinese models. The Trump administration is reportedly considering effectively barring Americans from using Chinese A.I. models. But banning those models would impede American developers and hand China the claim that its technology is too good for America to compete with fairly. The United States dominates in tech by making its platforms the ones the world’s developers choose to build on, not by banning foreign use. 两个国会委员会已就Airbnb和Cursor的母公司使用中国模型一事 展开调查 。据报道，特朗普政府正在考虑有效禁止美国人使用中国人工智能模型的措施。但是，禁止这些模型将给美国开发者带来不便，也会给中国提供口实，宣称它的技术先进到美国都无法通过公平竞争来应对。美国在科技领域的主导地位，靠的是让全球开发者都愿意基于美国的平台进行开发，而不是通过禁止外国使用来达成的。 The U.S. government should fund a contract to train an advanced open-weight model. It should stipulate those weights remain permanently open. That contract would give companies in the United States and allied nations a foundation to build on and compete in this arena of A.I. development. OpenAI and Google have released open-weight models, but only occasionally, because nothing rewards them for doing it consistently. The buyers of such a model would be the firms already reaching for Qwen and Kimi as well as the international partners that will not put their data on Chinese servers. 美国政府应当出资建立一个训练先进开放权重模型的项目，并规定这些权重必须永久保持开放。这将为美国及其盟友国家的企业提供一个共同的基础平台，使它们能够在人工智能发展的这一领域展开创新与竞争。 OpenAI 和 Google 都发布过开放权重模型，但只是偶尔为之，因为没有任何机制能激励它们持续这样做。这类模型的潜在用户不仅包括那些已经开始采用通义千问和Kimi的企业，也包括那些不愿把数据存放在中国服务器上的国际合作伙伴 Customers that adopt an open-weight American model also need the chips to run it, somewhere to store data and the computing power to put the model to work. That is what the Development Finance Corporation and the Export-Import Bank — the government agencies that back U.S. business abroad — should be financing all at once. Chinese models have come to dominate in places like Nairobi and São Paulo because China made them free, packaging the model, the hardware and the financing together. America has the capital and the technology to offer the same package, on better terms, with security standards that even newcomers can meet. 采用美国开放权重模型的用户同样需要运行模型所需的芯片、存储数据的基础设施，以及让模型真正投入使用所需的算力。这正是美国国际开发金融公司和美国进出口银行——这两个负责支持美国企业开展海外业务的政府机构——应当同时提供融资支持的方向。中国的模型之所以能够在内罗毕、圣保罗等地占据主导地位，是因为中国免费提供模型，并将模型、硬件和融资打包在一起。美国拥有足够的资金和技术，完全能够提供同样的整体方案，而且条件更优、安全标准更高，即使是刚起步的国家也能够达到这些标准。 OpenAI and Anthropic’s business is the “frontier”: the hardest, highest-value work, offered to customers that want the best model available and will pay for it. That is not the business an open-weight model takes, where finances or data-sensitivity factor in more heavily. For many U.S. customers, the frontier model keeps the hard work moving, and something cheaper — and easier to tinker with — sits underneath it. The frontier lab gets paid either way. OpenAI和Anthropic的商业模式立足于“前沿”，也就是承担最困难、价值最高工作的模型，服务对象是那些希望获得当前最优秀模型、并愿意为此付费的客户。开放权重模型面向的并非同一市场——在那里，财务成本或数据敏感性的考量权重更大。对许多美国用户而言，前沿模型负责完成最复杂的任务，而底层则运行着一种更便宜、也更容易进行定制修改的模型。无论哪种情况，前沿模型开发企业都能够获得收益。 The only question is whose model is underneath. It should be an American one. 唯一的问题是：那个底层模型来自哪里。答案应该是美国。 Jason Hsu是哈德逊研究所的高级研究员。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: “蟑螂”的愤怒：印度爆发大规模青年抗议
description: PRAGATI K.B., ANUPREETA DAS, ALEX TRAVELLI2026年7月22日周二，在新德里主要抗议现场，一些受伤的抗议者。他们誓言将继续抗争，以争取包括要求印度教育部长辞职在内的各项诉求。 Adnan Abidi/Reuters They flocked to New Delhi by the thousands. Young Indians demanding accountability from their government for a flawed education system, hoping for a promise or a signal from those in power that would reassure them about their futures. 数以千计的人涌向新德里。这些年轻的印度人要求政府对有缺陷的教育体系承担责任，希望能从当权者那里得到一个承诺或信号，让他们对自己的未来重拾信心。 Instead, the throng of protesters who tried to march to Parliament on Monday were confronted by security forces, batons in hand, tear gas canisters ready. As the crowd swelled, the police cracked down, striking people’s shins, calves and backs, swinging their staves overheard. Protesters hurled flip flops and water bottles back. Many rushed to escape through back alleys and side roads. Plumes of tear gas left people choking. 然而，周一试图游行前往议会的大批抗议者却遭遇了手持警棍和催泪瓦斯罐待命的安全部队。随着人群不断壮大，警方开始镇压，他们高举警棍，击打人们的小腿胫骨、腿肚子和背部。抗议者则予以回击，向警方投掷人字拖和水瓶。许多人匆忙从后巷和小路逃离。弥漫的催泪瓦斯呛得人们喘不过气来。 The protesters — mostly young people who chanted slogans, carried posters or stood quietly in solidarity — said they were shocked by the police crackdown and the lack of any real government response. By Tuesday, their sense of anger remained palpable as thousands returned to the protest site near Jantar Mantar, an 18th century observatory, undeterred by spurts of monsoon rain. 抗议者大多数是高呼口号、举着标语牌或静静站立以示团结的年轻人，他们表示，警方的镇压以及政府没有做出任何实质性回应令他们感到震惊。到了周二，他们的愤怒情绪依然显而易见，数以千计的人不顾季风带来的阵雨，重返位于18世纪天文台简塔·曼塔附近的抗议现场。 Security forces had removed tents and parts of the main stage at the venue. But Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party — a satirical movement that has become a vehicle for the frustrations of millions of young Indians — said that the protest will continue indefinitely. He implored people to keep it peaceful. 安全部队已经拆除了现场的帐篷和主舞台的部分设施。但“蟑螂人民党”的创始人阿比吉特·迪普克表示，抗议活动将无限期地继续下去。他恳求人们保持和平。该党是一个讽刺性运动，已成为数百万计印度年轻人宣泄不满的渠道。 Leaders of the C.J.P. said 150 protesters were taken to the hospital from injuries in the protest on Monday. The Delhi Police said 118 of its officers were injured during “violent protests.” Around 70 protesters were detained, according to lawyers’ groups. 蟑螂人民党的领导人表示，在周一的抗议活动中，有150名抗议者因伤被送往医院。德里警方表示，在“暴力抗议”期间，有118名警察受伤。据律师团体称，约有70名抗议者被拘留。 周一在新德里抗议活动现场的示威者。周一，一名警察向抗议者投掷了一枚催泪瓦斯。 Although Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not responded publicly to the protests, on Tuesday he spoke through an emissary. Kiren Rijiju, the parliamentary affairs minister, told reporters, “The safety, security and future of our youth are our priority.” 尽管总理莫迪尚未对抗议活动作出公开回应，但他在周二通过一名特使发表了讲话。议会事务部长基伦·里吉朱告诉记者：“我们年轻人的安全、保障和未来是我们的首要任务。” He also provided assurances that future paper leaks would be prevented. 他还保证，未来将防止试卷泄露事件再次发生。 Mr. Modi rarely responds to critics, so the comments appear to be a sign of the importance the leader has placed on the youth protests and a tacit acknowledgment of the political risk of alienating young voters in a country where more than 40 percent of the population is under the age of 25. 莫迪很少回应批评者，因此这些言论似乎表明这位领导人对青年抗议活动的重视，并且默认了，在一个25岁以下人口超过40%的国家里，疏远年轻选民会带来政治风险。 However, the government has said little in response to the specific demands of the C.J.P., which include the resignation of India’s education minister, whom the C.J.P. holds directly accountable for a shoddy education system and leaks in recent entrance exam papers that forced millions of students to retake their tests. 然而，对于蟑螂人民党的具体诉求，政府几乎没有作出任何回应。这些诉求包括要求印度教育部长辞职——该党认为他应对糟糕的教育体系以及近期入学考试试卷泄露事件负有直接责任，泄题事件迫使数百万学生重考。 “The government is in no mood to understand us and talk to us,” Chandan Mandal, a 19-year-old high school senior from the state of Rajasthan, said on Tuesday. He said he first protested more than a month ago. According to the C.J.P., at least 21 students have died by suicide since the exam leak, unable to handle the stress. “政府没有心情理解我们、和我们对话，”来自拉贾斯坦邦的19岁高中三年级学生钱丹·曼达尔周二表示。他说他第一次抗议是在一个多月前。据蟑螂人民党称，自试卷泄露事件以来，已有至少21名学生因无法承受压力而自杀。 The police struck him with a baton three times on Monday, Mr. Mandal said. Two reddish bruises, each about three inches long, and an open wound were visible on his back. 曼达尔说，警察周一用警棍打了他三次。在他的背上可以看到两块约七厘米长的微红瘀伤和一处开放性伤口。 “I’m opposing the government itself now,” said Mr. Mandal, who is studying for an entrance exam for engineering school. “我现在反对的是政府本身，”正在为工程学院入学考试做准备的曼达尔说。 来自拉贾斯坦邦的19岁高中应届毕业生钱丹·曼达尔表示，他在周一的抗议活动中受了伤。 Pragati K.B./The New York Times A big reason for the frustration millions of young Indians feel is that there aren’t enough jobs, or that there is a mismatch between available jobs and qualifications, according to economists. A recent, widely cited study from Azim Premji University found that 40 percent of young people under 25 are unemployed, even as access to higher education has increased. 经济学家表示，数以百万计的印度年轻人感到不满的一个重要原因是就业机会不足，或者现有工作与学历资质不匹配。阿齐姆·普雷姆吉大学最近一项被广泛引用的研究发现，尽管接受高等教育的机会增加了，但25岁以下的年轻人中有40%处于失业状态。 The protesters’ most visible slogans as they gathered on Monday morning were less concerned with botched exams than with the government’s overall accountability. 周一上午抗议者聚集时，最引人瞩目的口号与其说是关注搞砸的考试，不如说是关注政府的整体问责。 “India is a Democracy! We Need Answers!” read one, in English. “In Search of the Misguided,” read another, in Hindi, next to a hand-drawn sketch of Mr. Modi. 一条英文标语写道：“印度是一个民主国家！我们需要答案！”另一条印地语标语写着：“寻找被误导的人”，旁边是手绘的莫迪素描。 By the afternoon, the police waded in. Cries of pain rose above the shrill police whistles and sirens of riot control vans. A thin, young woman crouched on a median, as her friends dressed a fresh wound on her forearm and rinsed her face, reddened by tear gas. 到了下午，警察介入了。痛苦的呼喊声盖过了刺耳的警笛和防暴车的警报声。一名瘦弱的年轻女子蹲在马路中间的隔离带上，她的朋友们正在包扎她前臂上的新伤口，清洗她被催泪瓦斯熏红的脸。 At the Janpath subway station nearby, a police van lay overturned on its side, its windshield smashed. 在附近的詹帕特地铁站，一辆警车侧翻倒地，挡风玻璃被砸碎。 Further away from the violence, Wishwas Srivastav, 36, an engine builder, said he had traveled to Delhi from the state of Himachal Pradesh to join the protests. 在远离暴力冲突的地方，36岁的发动机制造工维什瓦斯·斯里瓦斯塔瓦说，他从喜马偕尔邦来到德里参加抗议活动。 “It hasn’t been feeling like democracy here for the past 10 or 15 years,” said Mr. Srivastav. Of the government, he said, “I hope they’re listening.” “在过去10年或15年里，这里感觉已经不像民主社会了，”斯里瓦斯塔瓦说。在谈到政府时，他说：“我希望他们能听进去。” 周一，一名警察试图用警棍驱散抗议者。警员们正在扶正一辆翻倒的警车。 By Tuesday morning, traffic along Janpath was back to normal, with some of the cross-streets more tightly barricaded. The police van at the metro station had been flipped upright. 到了周二早上，詹帕特的交通恢复了正常，一些十字路口设置了更严密的路障。地铁站旁的警车已被翻转扶正。 At the protest site, volunteers distributed food and drinks to protesters, including burgers from McDonald’s, samosas, water and electrolytes. 在抗议现场，志愿者向抗议者分发食物和饮料，包括麦当劳汉堡、萨莫萨咖喱角、水和电解质饮料。 Abhishek Kumar, 20, sat in the shade, tired after a roughly eight-hour bus ride from his hometown of Kanpur. After watching the protests on social media on Monday and seeing the police beat protesters, he said, he decided to join in person. Mr. Kumar, who recently took an entrance exam to join the armed forces, said he would stay for a few days. 20岁的阿布舍克·库马尔坐在阴凉处，他从家乡坎普尔乘坐了大约八小时的公共汽车赶到这里，显得很疲惫。他说，周一通过社交媒体观看了抗议活动并看到警察殴打抗议者后，他决定亲自加入。库马尔最近刚参加了武装部队的准入考试，他表示自己会在这里待上几天。 Many who gathered were parents worried about the future their children stand to inherit. Mina Ganesh, 51, was at the protest site on Tuesday with her son Miher, 17. 聚集在现场的有很多忧心忡忡的父母，他们担心孩子们的未来。51岁的米娜·加内什周二和她17岁的儿子米希尔一同来到抗议现场。 “Finally someone in the country is willing to speak up,” Ms. Ganesh said. “It took us long enough. Now that we have begun to speak up, there’s no stopping us.” “在这个国家里终于有人愿意发声了，”加内什说。“我们等得够久了。既然我们已经开始发声，就没有什么能阻止我们。” Miher, who wants to study either economics or engineering, said he was moved by the actions of Sonam Wangchuk, a prominent education activist who has backed the C.J.P.’s demands and joined its protest with a hunger strike. 米希尔希望攻读经济学或工程学，他被著名教育活动家索南·旺楚克的行为所感动。旺楚克支持蟑螂人民党的诉求，并通过绝食抗议加入了他们的行列。 Mr. Wangchuk is now 23 days into his fast and was forcibly moved to a hospital on Saturday by the government. 旺楚克目前的绝食抗议已进入第23天，他于周六被政府强行送往医院。 “He doesn’t know any of us,” Miher said. “How can I sit at home knowing he’ll die for me?” “他不认识我们当中任何一个人，”米希尔说。“明知他会为我而死，我怎么还能坐在家里无动于衷？” Pragati K.B.是时报驻新德里记者，报道印度各地新闻。 Anupreeta Das为时报报道印度和南亚新闻，常驻新德里。 Alex Travelli是驻新德里记者，报道印度和南亚其他地区的商业和经济发展。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。

Plumes of tear gas left people choking. 然而，周一试图游行前往议会的大批抗议者却遭遇了手持警棍和催泪瓦斯罐待命的安全部队。随着人群不断壮大，警方开始镇压，他们高举警棍，击打人们的小腿胫骨、腿肚子和背部。抗议者则予以回击，向警方投掷人字拖和水瓶。许多人匆忙从后巷和小路逃离。弥漫的催泪瓦斯呛得人们喘不过气来。 The protesters — mostly young people who chanted slogans, carried posters or stood quietly in solidarity — said they were shocked by the police crackdown and the lack of any real government response. By Tuesday, their sense of anger remained palpable as thousands returned to the protest site near Jantar Mantar, an 18th century observatory, undeterred by spurts of monsoon rain. 抗议者大多数是高呼口号、举着标语牌或静静站立以示团结的年轻人，他们表示，警方的镇压以及政府没有做出任何实质性回应令他们感到震惊。到了周二，他们的愤怒情绪依然显而易见，数以千计的人不顾季风带来的阵雨，重返位于18世纪天文台简塔·曼塔附近的抗议现场。 Security forces had removed tents and parts of the main stage at the venue. But Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party — a satirical movement that has become a vehicle for the frustrations of millions of young Indians — said that the protest will continue indefinitely. He implored people to keep it peaceful. 安全部队已经拆除了现场的帐篷和主舞台的部分设施。但“蟑螂人民党”的创始人阿比吉特·迪普克表示，抗议活动将无限期地继续下去。他恳求人们保持和平。该党是一个讽刺性运动，已成为数百万计印度年轻人宣泄不满的渠道。 Leaders of the C.J.P. said 150 protesters were taken to the hospital from injuries in the protest on Monday. The Delhi Police said 118 of its officers were injured during “violent protests.” Around 70 protesters were detained, according to lawyers’ groups. 蟑螂人民党的领导人表示，在周一的抗议活动中，有150名抗议者因伤被送往医院。德里警方表示，在“暴力抗议”期间，有118名警察受伤。据律师团体称，约有70名抗议者被拘留。 周一在新德里抗议活动现场的示威者。 周一，一名警察向抗议者投掷了一枚催泪瓦斯。 Although Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not responded publicly to the protests, on Tuesday he spoke through an emissary. Kiren Rijiju, the parliamentary affairs minister, told reporters, “The safety, security and future of our youth are our priority.” 尽管总理莫迪尚未对抗议活动作出公开回应，但他在周二通过一名特使发表了讲话。议会事务部长基伦·里吉朱告诉记者：“我们年轻人的安全、保障和未来是我们的首要任务。” He also provided assurances that future paper leaks would be prevented. 他还保证，未来将防止试卷泄露事件再次发生。 Mr. Modi rarely responds to critics, so the comments appear to be a sign of the importance the leader has placed on the youth protests and a tacit acknowledgment of the political risk of alienating young voters in a country where more than 40 percent of the population is under the age of 25. 莫迪很少回应批评者，因此这些言论似乎表明这位领导人对青年抗议活动的重视，并且默认了，在一个25岁以下人口超过40%的国家里，疏远年轻选民会带来政治风险。 However, the government has said little in response to the specific demands of the C.J.P., which include the resignation of India’s education minister, whom the C.J.P. holds directly accountable for a shoddy education system and leaks in recent entrance exam papers that forced millions of students to retake their tests. 然而，对于蟑螂人民党的具体诉求，政府几乎没有作出任何回应。这些诉求包括要求印度教育部长辞职——该党认为他应对糟糕的教育体系以及近期入学考试试卷泄露事件负有直接责任，泄题事件迫使数百万学生重考。 “The government is in no mood to understand us and talk to us,” Chandan Mandal, a 19-year-old high school senior from the state of Rajasthan, said on Tuesday. He said he first protested more than a month ago. According to the C.J.P., at least 21 students have died by suicide since the exam leak, unable to handle the stress. “政府没有心情理解我们、和我们对话，”来自拉贾斯坦邦的19岁高中三年级学生钱丹·曼达尔周二表示。他说他第一次抗议是在一个多月前。据蟑螂人民党称，自试卷泄露事件以来，已有至少21名学生因无法承受压力而自杀。 The police struck him with a baton three times on Monday, Mr. Mandal said. Two reddish bruises, each about three inches long, and an open wound were visible on his back. 曼达尔说，警察周一用警棍打了他三次。在他的背上可以看到两块约七厘米长的微红瘀伤和一处开放性伤口。 “I’m opposing the government itself now,” said Mr. Mandal, who is studying for an entrance exam for engineering school. “我现在反对的是政府本身，”正在为工程学院入学考试做准备的曼达尔说。 来自拉贾斯坦邦的19岁高中应届毕业生钱丹·曼达尔表示，他在周一的抗议活动中受了伤。 Pragati K.B./The New York Times A big reason for the frustration millions of young Indians feel is that there aren’t enough jobs, or that there is a mismatch between available jobs and qualifications, according to economists. A recent, widely cited study from Azim Premji University found that 40 percent of young people under 25 are unemployed, even as access to higher education has increased. 经济学家表示，数以百万计的印度年轻人感到不满的一个重要原因是就业机会不足，或者现有工作与学历资质不匹配。阿齐姆·普雷姆吉大学最近一项被广泛引用的研究发现，尽管接受高等教育的机会增加了，但25岁以下的年轻人中有40%处于失业状态。 The protesters’ most visible slogans as they gathered on Monday morning were less concerned with botched exams than with the government’s overall accountability. 周一上午抗议者聚集时，最引人瞩目的口号与其说是关注搞砸的考试，不如说是关注政府的整体问责。 “India is a Democracy! We Need Answers!” read one, in English. “In Search of the Misguided,” read another, in Hindi, next to a hand-drawn sketch of Mr. Modi. 一条英文标语写道：“印度是一个民主国家！我们需要答案！”另一条印地语标语写着：“寻找被误导的人”，旁边是手绘的莫迪素描。 By the afternoon, the police waded in. Cries of pain rose above the shrill police whistles and sirens of riot control vans. A thin, young woman crouched on a median, as her friends dressed a fresh wound on her forearm and rinsed her face, reddened by tear gas. 到了下午，警察介入了。痛苦的呼喊声盖过了刺耳的警笛和防暴车的警报声。一名瘦弱的年轻女子蹲在马路中间的隔离带上，她的朋友们正在包扎她前臂上的新伤口，清洗她被催泪瓦斯熏红的脸。 At the Janpath subway station nearby, a police van lay overturned on its side, its windshield smashed. 在附近的詹帕特地铁站，一辆警车侧翻倒地，挡风玻璃被砸碎。 Further away from the violence, Wishwas Srivastav, 36, an engine builder, said he had traveled to Delhi from the state of Himachal Pradesh to join the protests. 在远离暴力冲突的地方，36岁的发动机制造工维什瓦斯·斯里瓦斯塔瓦说，他从喜马偕尔邦来到德里参加抗议活动。 “It hasn’t been feeling like democracy here for the past 10 or 15 years,” said Mr. Srivastav. Of the government, he said, “I hope they’re listening.” “在过去10年或15年里，这里感觉已经不像民主社会了，”斯里瓦斯塔瓦说。在谈到政府时，他说：“我希望他们能听进去。” 周一，一名警察试图用警棍驱散抗议者。 警员们正在扶正一辆翻倒的警车。 By Tuesday morning, traffic along Janpath was back to normal, with some of the cross-streets more tightly barricaded. The police van at the metro station had been flipped upright. 到了周二早上，詹帕特的交通恢复了正常，一些十字路口设置了更严密的路障。地铁站旁的警车已被翻转扶正。 At the protest site, volunteers distributed food and drinks to protesters, including burgers from McDonald’s, samosas, water and electrolytes. 在抗议现场，志愿者向抗议者分发食物和饮料，包括麦当劳汉堡、萨莫萨咖喱角、水和电解质饮料。 Abhishek Kumar, 20, sat in the shade, tired after a roughly eight-hour bus ride from his hometown of Kanpur. After watching the protests on social media on Monday and seeing the police beat protesters, he said, he decided to join in person. Mr. Kumar, who recently took an entrance exam to join the armed forces, said he would stay for a few days. 20岁的阿布舍克·库马尔坐在阴凉处，他从家乡坎普尔乘坐了大约八小时的公共汽车赶到这里，显得很疲惫。他说，周一通过社交媒体观看了抗议活动并看到警察殴打抗议者后，他决定亲自加入。库马尔最近刚参加了武装部队的准入考试，他表示自己会在这里待上几天。 Many who gathered were parents worried about the future their children stand to inherit. Mina Ganesh, 51, was at the protest site on Tuesday with her son Miher, 17. 聚集在现场的有很多忧心忡忡的父母，他们担心孩子们的未来。51岁的米娜·加内什周二和她17岁的儿子米希尔一同来到抗议现场。 “Finally someone in the country is willing to speak up,” Ms. Ganesh said. “It took us long enough. Now that we have begun to speak up, there’s no stopping us.” “在这个国家里终于有人愿意发声了，”加内什说。“我们等得够久了。既然我们已经开始发声，就没有什么能阻止我们。” Miher, who wants to study either economics or engineering, said he was moved by the actions of Sonam Wangchuk, a prominent education activist who has backed the C.J.P.’s demands and joined its protest with a hunger strike. 米希尔希望攻读经济学或工程学，他被著名教育活动家索南·旺楚克的行为所感动。旺楚克支持蟑螂人民党的诉求，并通过绝食抗议加入了他们的行列。 Mr. Wangchuk is now 23 days into his fast and was forcibly moved to a hospital on Saturday by the government. 旺楚克目前的绝食抗议已进入第23天，他于周六被政府强行送往医院。 “He doesn’t know any of us,” Miher said. “How can I sit at home knowing he’ll die for me?” “他不认识我们当中任何一个人，”米希尔说。“明知他会为我而死，我怎么还能坐在家里无动于衷？” Pragati K.B. 是时报驻新德里记者，报道印度各地新闻。 Anupreeta Das 为时报报道印度和南亚新闻，常驻新德里。 Alex Travelli 是驻新德里记者，报道印度和南亚其他地区的商业和经济发展。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 从黑暗之海到自由之海：一个大胆逃离朝鲜的脱北者家族
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年7月22日金柳美（右）与两个孩子及母亲一同脱北。韩国的生活并非当初想象的样子，但他们丝毫不后悔离开朝鲜的残暴独裁和无休止的宣传。 Woohae Cho for The New York Times Rain lashed a flimsy wooden boat as it tossed through a churning sea, its engine straining against the swell. Under the cover of a stormy night three years ago, the vessel was fleeing North Korea. 三年前一个风雨交加的夜晚，一艘简陋的木船在汹涌的海浪中颠簸，雨水劈头盖脸地打来，发动机在涌浪中吃力轰鸣。借着夜色的掩护，这艘船正逃离朝鲜。 On board were nine people, including two small children and a woman who was six months pregnant. Only a couple of the passengers had seafaring experience. They eluded a patrol ship, speeding across the world’s most heavily guarded maritime border. 船上载着九个人，包括两个幼童和一名怀孕六个月的妇女。其中只有两三个人有航海经验。他们躲过了一艘巡逻船，加速穿越了世界上戒备最为森严的海上边界。 Soon after their boat lurched into South Korean waters, a high-speed warship of the South’s navy bore down on it, tearing the water in aggressive circles. Snipers on the vessel trained their laser sights on the chests of the three adult men on the wooden boat. 就在木船摇摇晃晃驶入韩国海域后不久，韩国海军的一艘高速战舰便迅速逼近，绕着木船划出咄咄逼人的圆弧。战舰上的狙击手将激光瞄准器锁定在木船上三名成年男子的胸口。 Through a loudspeaker, a voice boomed: “Are you lost? Engine trouble?” 扩音器中传来洪亮的声音：“你们是迷航了吗？还是发动机出故障了？” The North Koreans shouted: “Please help. We are defecting.” 船上的朝鲜人大喊：“请帮帮我们。我们是来投奔韩国的。” The red dots remained stubbornly fixed on their chests. The South Koreans were taking no chances: The three men were clad in North Korean military uniforms, camouflage for a high-stakes escape. Desperate, the men shouted into the boat’s cramped hold for the other passengers to emerge in order to prove that they were civilians. From below, the two children, a 5-year-old girl and 3-year-old boy, were hauled up first, both pale and wasted from seasickness. Only then did the red dots drop off. 然而，那几个红色激光点依然牢牢停留在他们胸前。韩国方面丝毫不敢掉以轻心，因为这三名男子都穿着朝鲜军装，那是他们为了这场生死逃亡而准备的伪装。情急之下，他们朝狭小的底舱里大喊，让其他人出来，以此证明他们都是平民。最先被拉上来的是两个孩子——一个五岁的女孩和一个三岁的男孩，两人因晕船而脸色苍白、有气无力的样子。直到这时，那几个红点才消失。 The North Koreans, led by Kim Il-hyeok and his younger brother, Yi-hyeok, were bound together by blood and marriage. The brothers, both in their 30s at the time, were accompanied by their mother and their families: Il-heyok’s partner, who was pregnant, and Yi-hyeok’s wife, their two children, his mother-in-law and brother-in-law. 这群朝鲜人由金日赫（音）和弟弟金李赫（音）率领，他们之间或者是血缘关系，或者是姻亲关系。当时兄弟俩都三十多岁，同行的还有他们的母亲以及各自的家人：金日赫怀有身孕的女友，金李赫的妻子、两个孩子、岳母和妻弟。 脱北者金日赫在首尔住处附近，摄于6月。他曾是韩流粉丝，在朝鲜时曾因“资本主义堕落行为”被捕。 The family, who defected in 2023, were among the few who managed to escape North Korea after its leader, Kim Jong-un, imposed a crushing lockdown during the coronavirus pandemic. They arrived in their adopted country with rare insights into a nation that had been choked off from the outside world. Some details of their escape have not been previously reported. 这一大家子于2023年脱北，是朝鲜领导人金正恩在新冠疫情期间实施严厉封锁后少数成功逃离朝鲜的人之一。他们来到新的家园，也带来了一个长期与外界隔绝国家的第一手见闻。他们出逃的部分细节此前从未公开报道过。 “That night,” said Yi-hyeok’s wife, Yu-mi, “we crossed from a sea of darkness to a sea of freedom.” “那天晚上，”金李赫的妻子柳美（音）说，“我们从黑暗之海穿越到了自由之海。” A Father’s Wish 父亲的心愿 Over several months of interviews in South Korea, Il-hyeok ​spoke with the same swagger that he had developed as a self-described “troublemaker” in North Korea. Yu-mi ​was reserved, pulling her legs tightly to her chest as she spoke. Her mother, who asked not to be named but agreed to be photographed, weighed every word, fearing how her comments might affect relatives left behind in the North. But they all spoke with conviction about why they had to leave North Korea. (The rest of the extended family declined to be interviewed.) 在韩国接受持续数月的采访期间，金日赫说话时仍带着那股他自认在朝鲜就是个“刺头”时练就的那股桀骜劲。柳美则显得拘谨，说话时总是双腿紧紧蜷在胸前。她的母亲同意接受采访和拍照，但要求不透露姓名，她每说一句话都十分谨慎，担心自己的言论会影响仍留在朝鲜的亲人。然而，他们都以坚定的语气讲述着自己为何不得不离开朝鲜。（其余的家族成员则拒绝接受采访。） The brothers came from Pyoksong, a county in North Korea’s southwest. 兄弟俩来自朝鲜西南部的碧城郡。 During the famine of the late 1990s, their father, a railway security official, returned with grim accounts from the hardest-hit provinces: The emaciated bodies of children found outside train stations were frozen solid, thumping like frozen fish when they were tossed onto trucks headed to burial grounds. He was the first in the family to lose faith in a ruling class that was unable to feed its people. 20世纪90年代末大饥荒期间，他们的父亲是铁路系统的安全员。他从饥荒最严重的省份回来时，讲述了令人毛骨悚然的见闻：火车站外面那些饿死的儿童瘦骨嶙峋，早已冻得僵硬，被扔上运往墓地的卡车时，像冻鱼一样发出闷响。父亲是家中第一个对这个连温饱都无法保障的统治阶级失去信心的人。 One night after his sons reached adulthood, he took them to a hill and pointed toward a cluster of lights across the South Korean border. 在两个儿子成年后的某个夜晚，他带着他们来到一座山坡上，指着韩国那侧密集的灯火。 “That’s where we should go,” he said. “To live and stand tall.” “我们应该去那里，”他说，“去活出个人样。” Yu-mi lived in the ​nearby coastal town of Kangryong. From there, she could see planes glinting in the sun as they rose from Incheon International Airport, just across the water — a shimmering vision of possibility, yet unreachable for North Koreans barred from travel and cut off from the internet. 柳美住在附近的沿海小镇康翎。在那里，她能看到对岸仁川国际机场起飞的飞机在阳光下闪闪发光——那是一幅闪耀着无限可能的景象，却是被禁止出国、与互联网隔绝的朝鲜人永远无法触及的世界。 “Our country felt like a prison without bars,” she said. “我们的国家就像一座没有围墙的监狱，”她说。 柳美与母亲，摄于6月。柳美形容，脱北是“从黑暗之海穿越到了自由之海”。 Beginning in kindergarten, children sang the anthem “We Have Nothing to Envy,” even as they were mobilized to haul river water or scour hills for herbs and pine nuts.​ After long workdays, adults attended compulsory “life review sessions,” writing self-criticism and pledges of loyalty. When Kim Jong-un visited ​an island near Yu-mi’s town in 2013, soldiers and villagers swarmed into the sea in jubilation. She knew the scene was staged; ordinary residents, she said, had been banned from leaving home. 从幼儿园开始，孩子们便要唱《世上没啥可羡慕》这首歌曲，同时还要组织去河边挑水，或到山上采草药、捡松子。成年人结束一天的劳动后，还必须参加“生活检讨会”，写自我批评和效忠保证书。2013年金正恩视察柳美老家附近的一座岛屿时，士兵和村民们纷纷涌入海中欢呼。她清楚这不过是在作秀——据她说，普通民众那天根本不许离开家门。 In the face of the propaganda, a contraband culture spread. South Korean films and dramas circulated on USB drives smuggled from China. In Kangryong, the devices also arrived inside plastic bottles released by South Korean activists across the water, along with rice and mini-Bibles. Officials warned the bottles contained poison, but South Korean entertainment was winning. 面对官方宣传，走私文化悄然蔓延。韩国电影和电视剧通过从中国走私进来的U盘在民间流传。在康翎，这些U盘也会随着韩国的活动人士从对岸投放的塑料瓶一起漂过来，瓶中还有大米和袖珍版《圣经》。官方警告大家瓶子里有毒，但韩国的娱乐节目依然深受欢迎。 Il-hyeok idolized K-pop groups like Girls’ Generation and styled his hair in a mohawk like BigBang’s Taeyang. He was arrested for “capitalist delinquency” and released only after paying a bribe, his hair razored. He and his friends once secretly watched “Valkyrie,” the Tom Cruise film about the plot to kill Hitler. When the conspirators failed and were executed, his friends wept. 大哥日赫崇拜“少女时代”等韩流组合，还把头发剃成了BigBang乐队成员太阳的同款莫西干造型。他因“资本主义堕落行为”被捕，行贿后才获释，头发被剃光。他和朋友曾偷偷观看汤姆·克鲁斯主演的电影《行动目标希特勒》。当刺杀计划失败、参与者被处决时，他的朋友们都哭了。 The brothers’ notion of deserting North Korea felt just as perilous. Their father forbade them from marrying, reasoning that the larger the family, the greater the risk of being caught while defecting. He then used connections to transfer Yi-hyeok, his youngest, to Kangryong, where he learned navigation, mapped guard posts, and cultivated ties with officials. Yi-hyeok became a helmet diver, who harvests seafood from the ocean floor, breathing fresh air piped through a surface hose. He eventually met Yu-mi. 兄弟俩逃离朝鲜的念头听起来同样凶险万分。父亲不许他们结婚，认为家庭成员越多，逃跑时暴露的风险就越大。随后他利用关系将小儿子调往康翎，在那里他学习了航海技术，绘制了岗哨分布图，并结交官员。金李赫成为了一名潜水员，在海底捕捞海产，靠连接水面的输气管呼吸。后来，他遇到了柳美。 Il-hyeok worked in North Korea’s shadow economy, bribing his way into opportunity and out of trouble. He butchered animals for restaurants, ran a small gold mine and bought rice stolen from state granaries, reselling it at a profit. He also grew disillusioned with the system he was gaming. 大哥日赫一直在朝鲜的地下经济中谋生，靠行贿获得机会，也靠行贿摆脱麻烦。他曾为餐馆屠宰牲畜，经营一个小金矿，还收购从国家粮库偷出来的大米，再转手获利。他也越来越厌倦这个自己一直在设法钻空子的制度。 Then, in 2014, their father died unexpectedly. The South Korean dream seemed to die with him. 然而，到了2014年，他们的父亲突然去世。去往韩国的梦想似乎也随之消散。 Where Il-hyeok, the older brother, was restless, Yi-hyeok was steady. He married Yu-mi in 2017, and the couple soon had their two children. He joined a military-run fisheries company, operating three vessels. Despite a United Nations ban, Chinese buyers worked openly in Kangryong, and on a good day Yi-hyeok could earn more than a typical worker​’s annual salary. 大哥日赫性格不安分，小弟李赫则沉稳踏实。2017年，李赫与柳美成婚，很快就有了两个孩子。他加入了一家军队经营的渔业公司，负责三艘渔船。尽管联合国明令禁止，中国买家仍公开活跃在康翎，运气好的日子，他一天的收入就能超过普通工人一年的薪水。 Il-hyeok began dating a kindergarten teacher. Defection was no longer a priority. 金日赫开始与一名幼儿园教师谈恋爱。逃离朝鲜不再是当务之急。 “When I mentioned it, my brother told me to watch my mouth,” Il-hyeok recalled. “每当我提起这件事，弟弟都会让我闭嘴，”日赫回忆道。 The pandemic overturned everything. 然而，疫情改变了一切。 Lockdown 封锁 North Korea imposed one of the world’s harshest lockdowns. In Kangryong, access to the sea was closed off with barbed wire and armed guards. Yi-hyeok’s boats rusted and his debts mounted. Officials claimed that South Korea was dumping infected bodies and waste into border waters. Yet boats supplying seafood to the top tiers of society continued to fish. 朝鲜实施了全球最严厉的疫情封锁措施之一。在康翎，通往海边的道路被铁丝网和武装警卫封锁。金李赫的渔船日渐锈蚀，债务越积越多。官方宣称，韩国向边境海域倾倒带有病毒的尸体和垃圾。但与此同时，专门供应高层海鲜的渔船却照常出海。 “The elites still ate whatever they wanted,” Yu-mi said. “那些有权有势的照样想吃什么就吃什么，”柳美说。 Public executions grew more frequent, targeting those accused of committing violent crimes like murder, which surged during the lockdown, or of distributing “nonsocialist” content such as South Korean dramas. Thousands, including the brothers, were forced to watch as rifle fire cracked across the execution grounds. The crowds dispersed in silence. 公开处决越来越频繁，处决对象包括那些被控犯有谋杀等暴力犯罪的人（这类案件在封锁期间激增），以及传播韩剧等“非社会主义内容”的人。包括兄弟俩在内，数千人被强迫观看处决，枪声在刑场不断响起。人群散去时，一片寂静。 “The goal was to instill fear,” Il-hyeok said. “To erase any fantasy about the outside world.” “目的就是制造恐惧，”大哥日赫说，“抹去人们对外部世界的一切幻想。” The Escape 逃离 The brothers no longer argued about whether to leave — only how. 两兄弟不再争论要不要走，只商量怎么走。 By early 2023, North Korea had begun easing its pandemic restrictions. Yi-hyeok’s boats were among the first permitted back to sea. But the window to escape was already closing. The authorities were preparing to install surveillance cameras along the coast to deter defections. 2023年初，朝鲜开始放宽疫情管控。金日赫的船是最早获准重返大海的渔船之一。但出逃的窗口也在迅速关闭——当局准备在沿海岸线安装监控摄像头，以遏制脱北行为。 The brothers spoke in code over the phone. “Good weather” meant a storm was coming, forcing patrol boats back to port. “We’ve got a good catch — come down here” meant Il-hyeok should bring their mother and his girlfriend to Kangryong. 兄弟俩在电话里用暗语交流。“天气好”意思是暴风雨要来了，巡逻船不得不回港。“今天收获不错，下来吧”意思是让大哥带着母亲和女友来康翎。 The weather and the catch were ideal the night of May 6, 2023. 2023年5月6日晚，天气和渔获都很理想。 Yu-mi’s mot​her, a 52-year-old widow, signed up last, just five hours before departure. 柳美52岁的寡母直到出发前五个小时才决定同行。 “I could die trying to escape,” she said. “But if my family reached the South and I stayed behind, I’d be as good as dead anyway — the relative of traitors.” “我可能会死在逃跑的路上，”她说，“但如果家人都到了韩国，只剩我留在朝鲜，那我也跟死了没什么区别——我会成为叛徒的家属。” Yi-hyeok’s brother-in-law, his fishing partner, slipped away by boat and waited offshore. The rest of the family crossed a coastal hill strewn with land mines to reach a secluded beach. To carry Yi-hyeok’s two young children more easily, the brothers sealed them inside burlap sacks and hoisted them onto their shoulders. Before they closed the sacks, Yu-mi caught her children looking up at her. 金李赫的妻弟——他的捕鱼搭档——先悄然驾船出海，在近海等候。其余家人翻越一座布满地雷的海岸山丘，来到一处僻静的海滩。为了方便，兄弟俩将弟弟李赫的两个年幼的孩子装进麻袋，扛在肩上。在麻袋合上之前，柳美看到孩子们抬头看着她。 “I thought it might be the last time I’d ever see them,” she said. “I cried, and my husband teared up, too.” “我当时想，这也许是我最后一次看见他们，”她说，“我哭了，丈夫也流下了眼泪。” Yi-hyeok’s brother-in-law spotted the prearranged signal — a flashlight blinking three times from the beach — and steered the boat in to pick up the rest of the extended family. Around 10 p.m., the 30-foot-long vessel pulled away, its engine throttled down to little more than a brisk walking pace as it tried to slip quietly toward Yeonpyeong Island in South Korea, just nine miles away. 金李赫的妻弟看到了预先约定的信号——海滩上有手电筒闪三下——便驾船靠近接上大家。晚上10点左右，这艘约九米长的船驶离岸边，引擎收小了油门，速度慢得几乎跟人快步走差不多，他们希望船能悄无声息地驶向仅14.5公里外的韩国延坪岛。 柳美展示部分逃亡路线。在她的家乡，可以看到从韩国仁川国际机场起飞的飞机在阳光下闪闪发光。 Below deck, Yu-mi suddenly felt ​the engine roar to full throttle, filling the hold with black exhaust and leaving the women and children seasick. Her youngest child’s eyes rolled back. She carried him up for fresh air — and found the men on deck in a panic. 在舱底，柳美突然感到引擎全速轰鸣起来，黑色的废气涌入船舱，女人和孩子们相继出现了晕船。最小的孩子翻起了白眼。她抱着孩子上来透气，却发现甲板上的男人们一片慌乱。 “That’s when I saw a searchlight from a North Korean patrol boat sweeping across the waves behind us,” she said. “My heart dropped.” “就在那时，我看到一艘朝鲜巡逻船的探照灯，正扫过我们身后的海面，”她说，“我的心沉了下去。” The brothers had already agreed on what to do if they couldn’t outrun a security vessel: strap life jackets and flashlights onto the women and children and send them into the sea, trusting the current to carry them south. The men would steer the boat away as a decoy, making a last stand with 20-inch knives and homemade red-pepper bombs. To lighten the boat, Il-hyeok threw anything heavy overboard — axes, wrenches, fishing net, his brother’s air compressor for helmet diving. 两兄弟早已商量好，万一甩不掉安全船该怎么办：给妇女和孩子套上救生衣，绑上手电筒，推进大海，依靠水流将他们带向南方。男人们则把船朝另一个方向开，吸引追兵，用半米长的刀和自制的辣椒炸弹做最后的抵抗。为了减轻载重，大哥日赫将所有重物扔进了大海——斧头、扳手、渔网，还有弟弟的潜水用空气压缩机。 Gradually, the searchlight behind them faded. The brothers later speculated that the fishing net they had thrown overboard had tangled in the pursuing boat’s propeller. 渐渐地，身后的探照灯消失了。兄弟俩后来推测，可能是他们丢下的渔网缠住了追船的螺旋桨。 Their two-hour gamble ended shortly after midnight, after the South Korean vessel stopped them and all nine family members were brought aboard. 这场历时两个小时的生死赌注在午夜过后不久画上了句点——韩国舰艇拦下了他们，九名家庭成员全部被带上了船。 An officer greeted them: “Welcome to paradise.” 一名军官迎上前来：“欢迎来到天堂。” New Beginning 新的开始 ​In the South, Yu-mi studied to gain an accounting clerk certificate and found work at a school. Her brother enrolled in college, while Yi-hyeok returned to helmet-diving for seafood. 在韩国，柳美通过努力学习拿到了会计助理证书，在一所学校找到了工作。她的弟弟上了大学，金李赫则重操旧业，从事海鲜的潜水采捞工作。 “My brother joked the diving gear here was so advanced he could fall asleep underwater if he wanted to,” Il-hyeok recalled. “我弟弟开玩笑说，这里的潜水设备太先进了，他要是愿意，甚至可以在海底睡觉。”大哥日赫回忆道。 Il-hyeok’s girlfriend gave birth to their first child in the South. The couple married in 2024 and soon welcomed another daughter. Il-hyeok is finding his footing in the South’s capitalist economy, trying part-time jobs at restaurants and operating forklifts and excavators. 金日赫的女友在韩国生下了他们的第一个孩子。2024年，两人成婚，不久又迎来了一个女儿。他正在努力适应韩国的资本主义经济，一边在餐厅打零工，一边开叉车和挖掘机。 The plunge into the South’s noisy democracy was overwhelming. Televisions offered endless channels — so different from the North, where only government broadcasts existed. Back home, Il-hyeok’s ​used motorbike was a prized status symbol​; now he found himself on highways crowded with modern cars. City squares rang with protests. 一开始，韩国喧闹的民主社会令他们无所适从。电视有数不清的频道，与朝鲜只有官方电视台形成鲜明对比。在朝鲜，金日赫那辆二手摩托车曾是令人艳羡的身份象征，如今他却置身于车水马龙的高速路上。城市广场上不断举行各种抗议活动。 Yu-mi’s mother marveled at faucets that produced both hot and cold water. On her first day working at a nursing home, ​she faltered when colleagues asked for “napkins” — another English word she had never heard. The brothers’ mother was scandalized by a TV drama in which a wife slapped her husband. And when Il-hyeok first ventured beyond Seoul, the South’s capital, he dutifully called a police detective to ask for permission. The detective only laughed. 柳美的母亲惊讶地发现，水龙头竟然既能放热水，也能放冷水。她第一天去养老院上班时，同事让她拿“napkins（餐巾纸）”，这个英语词她从来没听过，一时不知所措。兄弟俩的母亲则被一部电视剧里妻子扇丈夫耳光的情节震惊了。金日赫第一次去首尔以外的地方时，还规规矩矩地给警察打电话，请求批准，结果对方大笑起来。 And then there were elections. 还有选举。 In the North, ​people lined up in formal dress to receive a ballot with only one name. ​They placed ​their vote in the “yes” box with both hands and bowed deeply to portraits of Kim Jong-un’s father and grandfather, who ruled before him. No one dared approach the “no” box.​ When Il-hyeok and his wife voted in June as South Korean citizens, they found voters arriving in shorts and slippers, earphones in place. The ballot was a bewildering list of names. 在朝鲜，人们穿着正式服装排队领取选票，而选票上只有一个名字。他们必须双手把选票投入“赞成”箱，并向朝鲜曾经的统治者——金正恩的父亲和祖父的画像深深鞠躬。没有人敢靠近“反对”箱。而当金日赫和妻子今年6月作为韩国公民参加投票时，他们看到选民穿着短裤、拖鞋，戴着耳机就来投票，选票上密密麻麻印满了候选人姓名，令他们眼花缭乱。 Yet, South Korea was no paradise. 然而，韩国并非天堂。 After 19 months in the South, Yi-hyeok died in a diving accident in late 2024.​ The brothers’ mother and Il-hyeok’s wife were diagnosed with cancer. 来到韩国19个月后，弟弟李赫于2024年底在一次潜水事故中身亡。兄弟俩的母亲和日赫的妻子也相继被诊断出癌症。 Il-hyeok vented frustration at Seoul’s soaring housing prices. He is saving every penny to move his family out of their cramped, government-subsidized rental apartment. Still, he insisted the defection was “100 percent” the right choice.​ Before his death, Yi-hyeok appeared on television, explaining that he fled to spare his children the indoctrination of North Korean schools. His daughter is now a second grader at a South Korean school, and his son is in kindergarten. The children adapted fastest to their new lives, quickly embracing South Korean staples like fried chicken and pizza. 金日赫对首尔飞涨的房价满腹牢骚。他正拼命攒钱，希望带家人搬离现在这套狭小的政府廉租房。但他仍坚持认为，这次逃离“百分之百”是正确的选择。金李赫生前曾在电视节目中表示，他离开朝鲜是为了让孩子免受学校的洗脑教育。如今，他的女儿在韩国读小学二年级，儿子则在上幼儿园。两个孩子适应新生活的速度最快，很快就爱上了炸鸡和披萨等韩国日常美食。 “My husband gave me and our children the freedom he promised before he died,” Yu-mi said. “我丈夫兑现了他生前的承诺，把自由留给了我和孩子们，”柳美说。 The brothers also honored their father’s final wish: When their boat fled North Korea, they carried his ashes with them. 兄弟俩也兑现了父亲的遗愿：他们的船逃离朝鲜时，带上了父亲的骨灰。 金日赫展示他在首尔举行的婚礼的照片。他们脱北时，他现在的妻子已怀有六个月身孕。 Choe Sang-Hun是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: CHOE SANG-HUN 2026年7月22日 金柳美（右）与两个孩子及母亲一同脱北。韩国的生活并非当初想象的样子，但他们丝毫不后悔离开朝鲜的残暴独裁和无休止的宣传。 Woohae Cho for The New York Times Rain lashed a flimsy wooden boat as it tossed through a churning sea, its engine straining against the swell. Under the cover of a stormy night three years ago, the vessel was fleeing North Korea. 三年前一个风雨交加的夜晚，一艘简陋的木船在汹涌的海浪中颠簸，雨水劈头盖脸地打来，发动机在涌浪中吃力轰鸣。借着夜色的掩护，这艘船正逃离朝鲜。 On board were nine people, including two small children and a woman who was six months pregnant. Only a couple of the passengers had seafaring experience. They eluded a patrol ship, speeding across the world’s most heavily guarded maritime border. 船上载着九个人，包括两个幼童和一名怀孕六个月的妇女。其中只有两三个人有航海经验。他们躲过了一艘巡逻船，加速穿越了世界上戒备最为森严的海上边界。 Soon after their boat lurched into South Korean waters, a high-speed warship of the South’s navy bore down on it, tearing the water in aggressive circles. Snipers on the vessel trained their laser sights on the chests of the three adult men on the wooden boat. 就在木船摇摇晃晃驶入韩国海域后不久，韩国海军的一艘高速战舰便迅速逼近，绕着木船划出咄咄逼人的圆弧。战舰上的狙击手将激光瞄准器锁定在木船上三名成年男子的胸口。 Through a loudspeaker, a voice boomed: “Are you lost? Engine trouble?” 扩音器中传来洪亮的声音：“你们是迷航了吗？还是发动机出故障了？” The North Koreans shouted: “Please help. We are defecting.” 船上的朝鲜人大喊：“请帮帮我们。我们是来投奔韩国的。” The red dots remained stubbornly fixed on their chests. The South Koreans were taking no chances: The three men were clad in North Korean military uniforms, camouflage for a high-stakes escape. Desperate, the men shouted into the boat’s cramped hold for the other passengers to emerge in order to prove that they were civilians. From below, the two children, a 5-year-old girl and 3-year-old boy, were hauled up first, both pale and wasted from seasickness. Only then did the red dots drop off. 然而，那几个红色激光点依然牢牢停留在他们胸前。韩国方面丝毫不敢掉以轻心，因为这三名男子都穿着朝鲜军装，那是他们为了这场生死逃亡而准备的伪装。情急之下，他们朝狭小的底舱里大喊，让其他人出来，以此证明他们都是平民。最先被拉上来的是两个孩子——一个五岁的女孩和一个三岁的男孩，两人因晕船而脸色苍白、有气无力的样子。直到这时，那几个红点才消失。 The North Koreans, led by Kim Il-hyeok and his younger brother, Yi-hyeok, were bound together by blood and marriage. The brothers, both in their 30s at the time, were accompanied by their mother and their families: Il-heyok’s partner, who was pregnant, and Yi-hyeok’s wife, their two children, his mother-in-law and brother-in-law. 这群朝鲜人由金日赫（音）和弟弟金李赫（音）率领，他们之间或者是血缘关系，或者是姻亲关系。当时兄弟俩都三十多岁，同行的还有他们的母亲以及各自的家人：金日赫怀有身孕的女友，金李赫的妻子、两个孩子、岳母和妻弟。 脱北者金日赫在首尔住处附近，摄于6月。他曾是韩流粉丝，在朝鲜时曾因“资本主义堕落行为”被捕。 The family, who defected in 2023, were among the few who managed to escape North Korea after its leader, Kim Jong-un, imposed a crushing lockdown during the coronavirus pandemic. They arrived in their adopted country with rare insights into a nation that had been choked off from the outside world. Some details of their escape have not been previously reported. 这一大家子于2023年脱北，是朝鲜领导人金正恩在新冠疫情期间实施严厉封锁后少数成功逃离朝鲜的人之一。他们来到新的家园，也带来了一个长期与外界隔绝国家的第一手见闻。他们出逃的部分细节此前从未公开报道过。 “That night,” said Yi-hyeok’s wife, Yu-mi, “we crossed from a sea of darkness to a sea of freedom.” “那天晚上，”金李赫的妻子柳美（音）说，“我们从黑暗之海穿越到了自由之海。” A Father’s Wish 父亲的心愿 Over several months of interviews in South Korea, Il-hyeok ​spoke with the same swagger that he had developed as a self-described “troublemaker” in North Korea. Yu-mi ​was reserved, pulling her legs tightly to her chest as she spoke. Her mother, who asked not to be named but agreed to be photographed, weighed every word, fearing how her comments might affect relatives left behind in the North. But they all spoke with conviction about why they had to leave North Korea. (The rest of the extended family declined to be interviewed.) 在韩国接受持续数月的采访期间，金日赫说话时仍带着那股他自认在朝鲜就是个“刺头”时练就的那股桀骜劲。柳美则显得拘谨，说话时总是双腿紧紧蜷在胸前。她的母亲同意接受采访和拍照，但要求不透露姓名，她每说一句话都十分谨慎，担心自己的言论会影响仍留在朝鲜的亲人。然而，他们都以坚定的语气讲述着自己为何不得不离开朝鲜。（其余的家族成员则拒绝接受采访。） The brothers came from Pyoksong, a county in North Korea’s southwest. 兄弟俩来自朝鲜西南部的碧城郡。 During the famine of the late 1990s, their father, a railway security official, returned with grim accounts from the hardest-hit provinces: The emaciated bodies of children found outside train stations were frozen solid, thumping like frozen fish when they were tossed onto trucks headed to burial grounds. He was the first in the family to lose faith in a ruling class that was unable to feed its people. 20世纪90年代末大饥荒期间，他们的父亲是铁路系统的安全员。他从饥荒最严重的省份回来时，讲述了令人毛骨悚然的见闻：火车站外面那些饿死的儿童瘦骨嶙峋，早已冻得僵硬，被扔上运往墓地的卡车时，像冻鱼一样发出闷响。父亲是家中第一个对这个连温饱都无法保障的统治阶级失去信心的人。 One night after his sons reached adulthood, he took them to a hill and pointed toward a cluster of lights across the South Korean border. 在两个儿子成年后的某个夜晚，他带着他们来到一座山坡上，指着韩国那侧密集的灯火。 “That’s where we should go,” he said. “To live and stand tall.” “我们应该去那里，”他说，“去活出个人样。” Yu-mi lived in the ​nearby coastal town of Kangryong. From there, she could see planes glinting in the sun as they rose from Incheon International Airport, just across the water — a shimmering vision of possibility, yet unreachable for North Koreans barred from travel and cut off from the internet. 柳美住在附近的沿海小镇康翎。在那里，她能看到对岸仁川国际机场起飞的飞机在阳光下闪闪发光——那是一幅闪耀着无限可能的景象，却是被禁止出国、与互联网隔绝的朝鲜人永远无法触及的世界。 “Our country felt like a prison without bars,” she said. “我们的国家就像一座没有围墙的监狱，”她说。 柳美与母亲，摄于6月。柳美形容，脱北是“从黑暗之海穿越到了自由之海”。 Beginning in kindergarten, children sang the anthem “We Have Nothing to Envy,” even as they were mobilized to haul river water or scour hills for herbs and pine nuts.​ After long workdays, adults attended compulsory “life review sessions,” writing self-criticism and pledges of loyalty. When Kim Jong-un visited ​an island near Yu-mi’s town in 2013, soldiers and villagers swarmed into the sea in jubilation. She knew the scene was staged; ordinary residents, she said, had been banned from leaving home. 从幼儿园开始， 孩子们便要唱 《世上没啥可羡慕》这首歌曲，同时还要组织去河边挑水，或到山上采草药、捡松子。成年人结束一天的劳动后，还必须参加“生活检讨会”，写自我批评和效忠保证书。2013年金正恩视察柳美老家附近的一座岛屿时， 士兵和村民们纷纷涌入 海中欢呼。她清楚这不过是在作秀——据她说，普通民众那天根本不许离开家门。 In the face of the propaganda, a contraband culture spread. South Korean films and dramas circulated on USB drives smuggled from China. In Kangryong, the devices also arrived inside plastic bottles released by South Korean activists across the water, along with rice and mini-Bibles. Officials warned the bottles contained poison, but South Korean entertainment was winning. 面对官方宣传，走私文化悄然蔓延。韩国电影和电视剧通过从中国走私进来的U盘在民间流传。在康翎，这些U盘也会随着韩国的活动人士从对岸投放的塑料瓶一起漂过来，瓶中还有大米和袖珍版《圣经》。官方警告大家瓶子里有毒，但韩国的娱乐节目依然深受欢迎。 Il-hyeok idolized K-pop groups like Girls’ Generation and styled his hair in a mohawk like BigBang’s Taeyang . He was arrested for “capitalist delinquency” and released only after paying a bribe, his hair razored. He and his friends once secretly watched “Valkyrie,” the Tom Cruise film about the plot to kill Hitler. When the conspirators failed and were executed, his friends wept. 大哥日赫崇拜“少女时代”等韩流组合，还把头发剃成了 BigBang乐队成员太阳 的同款莫西干造型。他因“资本主义堕落行为”被捕，行贿后才获释，头发被剃光。他和朋友曾偷偷观看 汤姆·克鲁斯主演的电影 《行动目标希特勒》。当刺杀计划失败、参与者被处决时，他的朋友们都哭了。 The brothers’ notion of deserting North Korea felt just as perilous. Their father forbade them from marrying, reasoning that the larger the family, the greater the risk of being caught while defecting. He then used connections to transfer Yi-hyeok, his youngest, to Kangryong, where he learned navigation, mapped guard posts, and cultivated ties with officials. Yi-hyeok became a helmet diver, who harvests seafood from the ocean floor, breathing fresh air piped through a surface hose. He eventually met Yu-mi. 兄弟俩逃离朝鲜的念头听起来同样凶险万分。父亲不许他们结婚，认为家庭成员越多，逃跑时暴露的风险就越大。随后他利用关系将小儿子调往康翎，在那里他学习了航海技术，绘制了岗哨分布图，并结交官员。金李赫成为了一名潜水员，在海底捕捞海产，靠连接水面的输气管呼吸。后来，他遇到了柳美。 Il-hyeok worked in North Korea’s shadow economy, bribing his way into opportunity and out of trouble. He butchered animals for restaurants, ran a small gold mine and bought rice stolen from state granaries, reselling it at a profit. He also grew disillusioned with the system he was gaming. 大哥日赫一直在朝鲜的地下经济中谋生，靠行贿获得机会，也靠行贿摆脱麻烦。他曾为餐馆屠宰牲畜，经营一个小金矿，还收购从国家粮库偷出来的大米，再转手获利。他也越来越厌倦这个自己一直在设法钻空子的制度。 Then, in 2014, their father died unexpectedly. The South Korean dream seemed to die with him. 然而，到了2014年，他们的父亲突然去世。去往韩国的梦想似乎也随之消散。 Where Il-hyeok, the older brother, was restless, Yi-hyeok was steady. He married Yu-mi in 2017, and the couple soon had their two children. He joined a military-run fisheries company, operating three vessels. Despite a United Nations ban, Chinese buyers worked openly in Kangryong, and on a good day Yi-hyeok could earn more than a typical worker​’s annual salary. 大哥日赫性格不安分，小弟李赫则沉稳踏实。2017年，李赫与柳美成婚，很快就有了两个孩子。他加入了一家军队经营的渔业公司，负责三艘渔船。尽管联合国明令禁止，中国买家仍公开活跃在康翎，运气好的日子，他一天的收入就能超过普通工人一年的薪水。 Il-hyeok began dating a kindergarten teacher. Defection was no longer a priority. 金日赫开始与一名幼儿园教师谈恋爱。逃离朝鲜不再是当务之急。 “When I mentioned it, my brother told me to watch my mouth,” Il-hyeok recalled. “每当我提起这件事，弟弟都会让我闭嘴，”日赫回忆道。 The pandemic overturned everything. 然而，疫情改变了一切。 Lockdown 封锁 North Korea imposed one of the world’s harshest lockdowns. In Kangryong, access to the sea was closed off with barbed wire and armed guards. Yi-hyeok’s boats rusted and his debts mounted. Officials claimed that South Korea was dumping infected bodies and waste into border waters. Yet boats supplying seafood to the top tiers of society continued to fish. 朝鲜实施了全球最严厉的疫情封锁措施之一。在康翎，通往海边的道路被铁丝网和武装警卫封锁。金李赫的渔船日渐锈蚀，债务越积越多。官方宣称，韩国向边境海域倾倒带有病毒的尸体和垃圾。但与此同时，专门供应高层海鲜的渔船却照常出海。 “The elites still ate whatever they wanted,” Yu-mi said. “那些有权有势的照样想吃什么就吃什么，”柳美说。 Public executions grew more frequent, targeting those accused of committing violent crimes like murder, which surged during the lockdown, or of distributing “nonsocialist” content such as South Korean dramas. Thousands, including the brothers, were forced to watch as rifle fire cracked across the execution grounds. The crowds dispersed in silence. 公开处决越来越频繁，处决对象包括那些被控犯有谋杀等暴力犯罪的人（这类案件在封锁期间激增），以及传播韩剧等“非社会主义内容”的人。包括兄弟俩在内，数千人被强迫观看处决，枪声在刑场不断响起。人群散去时，一片寂静。 “The goal was to instill fear,” Il-hyeok said. “To erase any fantasy about the outside world.” “目的就是制造恐惧，”大哥日赫说，“抹去人们对外部世界的一切幻想。” The Escape 逃离 The brothers no longer argued about whether to leave — only how. 两兄弟不再争论要不要走，只商量怎么走。 By early 2023, North Korea had begun easing its pandemic restrictions. Yi-hyeok’s boats were among the first permitted back to sea. But the window to escape was already closing. The authorities were preparing to install surveillance cameras along the coast to deter defections. 2023年初，朝鲜开始放宽疫情管控。金日赫的船是最早获准重返大海的渔船之一。但出逃的窗口也在迅速关闭——当局准备在沿海岸线安装监控摄像头，以遏制脱北行为。 The brothers spoke in code over the phone. “Good weather” meant a storm was coming, forcing patrol boats back to port. “We’ve got a good catch — come down here” meant Il-hyeok should bring their mother and his girlfriend to Kangryong. 兄弟俩在电话里用暗语交流。“天气好”意思是暴风雨要来了，巡逻船不得不回港。“今天收获不错，下来吧”意思是让大哥带着母亲和女友来康翎。 The weather and the catch were ideal the night of May 6, 2023. 2023年5月6日晚，天气和渔获都很理想。 Yu-mi’s mot​her, a 52-year-old widow, signed up last, just five hours before departure. 柳美52岁的寡母直到出发前五个小时才决定同行。 “I could die trying to escape,” she said. “But if my family reached the South and I stayed behind, I’d be as good as dead anyway — the relative of traitors.” “我可能会死在逃跑的路上，”她说，“但如果家人都到了韩国，只剩我留在朝鲜，那我也跟死了没什么区别——我会成为叛徒的家属。” Yi-hyeok’s brother-in-law, his fishing partner, slipped away by boat and waited offshore. The rest of the family crossed a coastal hill strewn with land mines to reach a secluded beach. To carry Yi-hyeok’s two young children more easily, the brothers sealed them inside burlap sacks and hoisted them onto their shoulders. Before they closed the sacks, Yu-mi caught her children looking up at her. 金李赫的妻弟——他的捕鱼搭档——先悄然驾船出海，在近海等候。其余家人翻越一座布满地雷的海岸山丘，来到一处僻静的海滩。为了方便，兄弟俩将弟弟李赫的两个年幼的孩子装进麻袋，扛在肩上。在麻袋合上之前，柳美看到孩子们抬头看着她。 “I thought it might be the last time I’d ever see them,” she said. “I cried, and my husband teared up, too.” “我当时想，这也许是我最后一次看见他们，”她说，“我哭了，丈夫也流下了眼泪。” Yi-hyeok’s brother-in-law spotted the prearranged signal — a flashlight blinking three times from the beach — and steered the boat in to pick up the rest of the extended family. Around 10 p.m., the 30-foot-long vessel pulled away, its engine throttled down to little more than a brisk walking pace as it tried to slip quietly toward Yeonpyeong Island in South Korea, just nine miles away. 金李赫的妻弟看到了预先约定的信号——海滩上有手电筒闪三下——便驾船靠近接上大家。晚上10点左右，这艘约九米长的船驶离岸边，引擎收小了油门，速度慢得几乎跟人快步走差不多，他们希望船能悄无声息地驶向仅14.5公里外的韩国延坪岛。 柳美展示部分逃亡路线。在她的家乡，可以看到从韩国仁川国际机场起飞的飞机在阳光下闪闪发光。 Below deck, Yu-mi suddenly felt ​the engine roar to full throttle, filling the hold with black exhaust and leaving the women and children seasick. Her youngest child’s eyes rolled back. She carried him up for fresh air — and found the men on deck in a panic. 在舱底，柳美突然感到引擎全速轰鸣起来，黑色的废气涌入船舱，女人和孩子们相继出现了晕船。最小的孩子翻起了白眼。她抱着孩子上来透气，却发现甲板上的男人们一片慌乱。 “That’s when I saw a searchlight from a North Korean patrol boat sweeping across the waves behind us,” she said. “My heart dropped.” “就在那时，我看到一艘朝鲜巡逻船的探照灯，正扫过我们身后的海面，”她说，“我的心沉了下去。” The brothers had already agreed on what to do if they couldn’t outrun a security vessel: strap life jackets and flashlights onto the women and children and send them into the sea, trusting the current to carry them south. The men would steer the boat away as a decoy, making a last stand with 20-inch knives and homemade red-pepper bombs. To lighten the boat, Il-hyeok threw anything heavy overboard — axes, wrenches, fishing net, his brother’s air compressor for helmet diving. 两兄弟早已商量好，万一甩不掉安全船该怎么办：给妇女和孩子套上救生衣，绑上手电筒，推进大海，依靠水流将他们带向南方。男人们则把船朝另一个方向开，吸引追兵，用半米长的刀和自制的辣椒炸弹做最后的抵抗。为了减轻载重，大哥日赫将所有重物扔进了大海——斧头、扳手、渔网，还有弟弟的潜水用空气压缩机。 Gradually, the searchlight behind them faded. The brothers later speculated that the fishing net they had thrown overboard had tangled in the pursuing boat’s propeller. 渐渐地，身后的探照灯消失了。兄弟俩后来推测，可能是他们丢下的渔网缠住了追船的螺旋桨。 Their two-hour gamble ended shortly after midnight, after the South Korean vessel stopped them and all nine family members were brought aboard. 这场历时两个小时的生死赌注在午夜过后不久画上了句点——韩国舰艇拦下了他们，九名家庭成员全部被带上了船。 An officer greeted them: “Welcome to paradise.” 一名军官迎上前来：“欢迎来到天堂。” New Beginning 新的开始 ​In the South, Yu-mi studied to gain an accounting clerk certificate and found work at a school. Her brother enrolled in college, while Yi-hyeok returned to helmet-diving for seafood. 在韩国，柳美通过努力学习拿到了会计助理证书，在一所学校找到了工作。她的弟弟上了大学，金李赫则重操旧业，从事海鲜的潜水采捞工作。 “My brother joked the diving gear here was so advanced he could fall asleep underwater if he wanted to,” Il-hyeok recalled. “我弟弟开玩笑说，这里的潜水设备太先进了，他要是愿意，甚至可以在海底睡觉。”大哥日赫回忆道。 Il-hyeok’s girlfriend gave birth to their first child in the South. The couple married in 2024 and soon welcomed another daughter. Il-hyeok is finding his footing in the South’s capitalist economy, trying part-time jobs at restaurants and operating forklifts and excavators. 金日赫的女友在韩国生下了他们的第一个孩子。2024年，两人成婚，不久又迎来了一个女儿。他正在努力适应韩国的资本主义经济，一边在餐厅打零工，一边开叉车和挖掘机。 The plunge into the South’s noisy democracy was overwhelming. Televisions offered endless channels — so different from the North, where only government broadcasts existed. Back home, Il-hyeok’s ​used motorbike was a prized status symbol​; now he found himself on highways crowded with modern cars. City squares rang with protests. 一开始，韩国喧闹的民主社会令他们无所适从。电视有数不清的频道，与朝鲜只有官方电视台形成鲜明对比。在朝鲜，金日赫那辆二手摩托车曾是令人艳羡的身份象征，如今他却置身于车水马龙的高速路上。城市广场上不断举行各种抗议活动。 Yu-mi’s mother marveled at faucets that produced both hot and cold water. On her first day working at a nursing home, ​she faltered when colleagues asked for “napkins” — another English word she had never heard. The brothers’ mother was scandalized by a TV drama in which a wife slapped her husband. And when Il-hyeok first ventured beyond Seoul, the South’s capital, he dutifully called a police detective to ask for permission. The detective only laughed. 柳美的母亲惊讶地发现，水龙头竟然既能放热水，也能放冷水。她第一天去养老院上班时，同事让她拿“napkins（餐巾纸）”，这个英语词她从来没听过，一时不知所措。兄弟俩的母亲则被一部电视剧里妻子扇丈夫耳光的情节震惊了。金日赫第一次去首尔以外的地方时，还规规矩矩地给警察打电话，请求批准，结果对方大笑起来。 And then there were elections. 还有选举。 In the North, ​people lined up in formal dress to receive a ballot with only one name. ​They placed ​their vote in the “yes” box with both hands and bowed deeply to portraits of Kim Jong-un’s father and grandfather, who ruled before him. No one dared approach the “no” box.​ When Il-hyeok and his wife voted in June as South Korean citizens, they found voters arriving in shorts and slippers, earphones in place. The ballot was a bewildering list of names. 在朝鲜，人们穿着正式服装排队领取选票，而选票上只有一个名字。他们必须双手把选票投入“赞成”箱，并向朝鲜曾经的统治者——金正恩的父亲和祖父的画像深深鞠躬。没有人敢靠近“反对”箱。而当金日赫和妻子今年6月作为韩国公民参加投票时，他们看到选民穿着短裤、拖鞋，戴着耳机就来投票，选票上密密麻麻印满了候选人姓名，令他们眼花缭乱。 Yet, South Korea was no paradise. 然而，韩国并非天堂。 After 19 months in the South, Yi-hyeok died in a diving accident in late 2024.​ The brothers’ mother and Il-hyeok’s wife were diagnosed with cancer. 来到韩国19个月后，弟弟李赫于2024年底在一次潜水事故中身亡。兄弟俩的母亲和日赫的妻子也相继被诊断出癌症。 Il-hyeok vented frustration at Seoul’s soaring housing prices. He is saving every penny to move his family out of their cramped, government-subsidized rental apartment. Still, he insisted the defection was “100 percent” the right choice.​ Before his death, Yi-hyeok appeared on television, explaining that he fled to spare his children the indoctrination of North Korean schools. His daughter is now a second grader at a South Korean school, and his son is in kindergarten. The children adapted fastest to their new lives, quickly embracing South Korean staples like fried chicken and pizza. 金日赫对首尔飞涨的房价满腹牢骚。他正拼命攒钱，希望带家人搬离现在这套狭小的政府廉租房。但他仍坚持认为，这次逃离“百分之百”是正确的选择。金李赫生前曾在电视节目中表示，他离开朝鲜是为了让孩子免受学校的洗脑教育。如今，他的女儿在韩国读小学二年级，儿子则在上幼儿园。两个孩子适应新生活的速度最快，很快就爱上了炸鸡和披萨等韩国日常美食。 “My husband gave me and our children the freedom he promised before he died,” Yu-mi said. “我丈夫兑现了他生前的承诺，把自由留给了我和孩子们，”柳美说。 The brothers also honored their father’s final wish: When their boat fled North Korea, they carried his ashes with them. 兄弟俩也兑现了父亲的遗愿：他们的船逃离朝鲜时，带上了父亲的骨灰。 金日赫展示他在首尔举行的婚礼的照片。他们脱北时，他现在的妻子已怀有六个月身孕。 Choe Sang-Hun 是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 鲁比奥与王毅就习近平9月访美事宜进行磋商
description: 黄安伟2026年7月23日5月，特朗普总统在北京与习近平会面。 Kenny Holston/The New York Times Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he spoke with China’s top diplomat on Wednesday about a state visit scheduled for September by Xi Jinping, China’s leader, to Washington, where President Trump intends to try to bolster what he sees as a personal friendship the two men are developing. 国务卿鲁比奥表示，他周三与中国最高外交官就中国领导人习近平定于9月对华盛顿进行的国事访问进行了磋商。特朗普总统打算借此机会努力巩固他眼中两人正在建立的个人友谊。 The fact that the two nations’ top diplomats spent much of a meeting in Manila talking about the visit is the strongest sign yet that the summit is on schedule, despite remarks last week from Mr. Trump blaming China for trying to interfere in American elections. 在马尼拉的会晤中，两国最高外交官将大部分时间用于讨论此次访问。这是迄今为止最为强烈的信号，表明峰会正在按计划进行，尽管特朗普上周发表言论，指责中国试图干预美国选举。 “It’s just to create the groundwork for another positive visit,” Mr. Rubio said of his talk with Wang Yi after it ended in the evening after more than an hour. “I think President Xi will have a very positive visit when he comes to Washington.” “这只是为了给又一次积极的访问奠定基础，”鲁比奥在晚上结束了与王毅一个多小时的会谈后这样评价。“我认为习近平主席来到华盛顿时，将进行一次非常积极的访问。” He said that the two governments were putting in place a board of trade and a separate board of investment, and that more details would be announced during the September summit. The two leaders agreed to establish the groups when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May, more than half a year after he had to retreat from a trade war he had started with China. 他表示，两国政府正在设立一个贸易委员会和一个独立的投资委员会，更多细节将在9月的峰会上公布。今年5月特朗普访问北京时，两国领导人同意成立这两个机构，此时距离特朗普被迫从自己挑起的对华贸易战中退却，已过去了半年多。 Mr. Rubio told reporters traveling with him that he and Mr. Wang did not talk about Mr. Trump’s recent accusations that China had tried to interfere in U.S. elections, mainly in 2020. The intelligence material that Mr. Trump brought up in a speech last Thursday was not new and had been reviewed by U.S. officials years ago. U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that Russia is the main rival that has tried to interfere in American elections. 鲁比奥告诉随行记者，他与王毅没有谈论特朗普最近关于中国试图干预美国选举（主要是在2020年）的指控。特朗普在上周四的演讲中提到的情报材料并不新鲜，几年前就已被美国官员审阅。美国情报机构得出的结论是，俄罗斯才是试图干预美国选举的主要对手。 周三，美国国务卿鲁比奥（右）在马尼拉与中国外交部长王毅（左）举行了双边会晤。 The Chinese foreign ministry has given pro forma statements pushing back on Mr. Trump’s accusations. But it has also indicated that Chinese officials understand that the American president made his speech for the purposes of domestic politics rather than out of actual foreign policy concerns. 中国外交部发表了例行声明，反驳特朗普的指控。但中方也暗示，中国官员知道美国总统发表该演讲是出于国内政治目的，而不是出于实际的外交政策顾虑。 “Obviously, there are areas of great differences,” Mr. Rubio said of U.S.-China relations. “Both sides will acknowledge that we’ll have to work through those, and I think these differences will exist for the foreseeable future.” “显然，双方在一些领域存在巨大分歧，”鲁比奥在谈到美中关系时说。“双方都会承认，我们必须解决这些问题，而且我认为这些分歧在可预见的未来仍将存在。” Mr. Rubio was in Manila for an annual conference of top diplomats from Southeast Asian nations. Mr. Wang and Sergey Lavrov, Russia’s top diplomat, are also in Manila this week. 鲁比奥当时在马尼拉参加东南亚国家最高外交官年度会议。王毅和俄罗斯最高外交官拉夫罗夫本周也在马尼拉。 Mr. Rubio accompanied Mr. Trump on his visit to Beijing in May, where Mr. Xi showered the American president with flattery — even saying he supported the “Make America Great Again” movement — and hosted a state banquet. A video showed Mr. Rubio marveling at the ceiling of a meeting room in the Great Hall of the People, next to Tiananmen Square. During his 14 years as a senator representing Florida, Mr. Rubio became one of the leading China hawks in Congress, but he has since tempered his tone to stay in alignment with Mr. Trump. 卢比奥曾在5月陪同特朗普访问北京，期间习近平对美国总统大加赞誉——甚至表示支持“让美国再次伟大”运动——并举办了国宴。一段视频显示，鲁比奥在天安门广场旁的人民大会堂的一个会议室里，对天花板赞叹不已。在担任代表佛罗里达州的参议员的14年间，鲁比奥曾是国会中主要的对华鹰派人物之一，但此后他缓和了语气，与特朗普保持一致。 In the Manila meeting with Mr. Rubio, Mr. Wang protested “recent negative remarks and actions by the U.S. side,” but also hailed the leadership summit in Beijing, according to an official summary of the talks posted by Xinhua, the Chinese state news agency. “Our responsibility now is to follow the course set by the two heads of state,” Mr. Wang said. 根据中国国家通讯社新华社发布的会谈官方摘要，在马尼拉与鲁比奥的会晤中，王毅对“近期美方的一系列消极言行”表示抗议，但也高度评价了北京的领导人峰会。“现在我们的责任是，沿着两国元首设定的轨道，”王毅说。 Mr. Rubio was asked by a reporter whether China and Russia were giving information to Iran to help the Iranian military fire projectiles at U.S. troops, as some U.S. officials have said was happening. Mr. Rubio did not give a direct answer. 有记者问鲁比奥，中俄两国是否如一些美国官员所称的那样，正在向伊朗提供信息，帮助伊朗军队向美军发射弹药。鲁比奥没有给出直接回答。 “Nothing that’s happened, nothing that China has done, has in any way changed the trajectory of what you’re seeing in terms of the conflicts we’re having with Iran,” he said. “没有发生任何事情、也没有中国采取的任何行动在任何方面改变了你们所看到的我们与伊朗冲突的进程，”他说。 Mr. Rubio said China is unhappy with Iran’s attacks on commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for the transport of oil and gas to China and many other countries. 鲁比奥表示，中国对伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡袭击商业油轮感到不满，该海峡是向中国和其他许多国家运输石油和天然气的关键水道。 Mr. Rubio did criticize recent aggressive encroachments by Chinese coast guard ships into waters near Taiwan. In recent years, China has increased its naval and aerial military operations around Taiwan, a de facto independent island that Mr. Xi has said must eventually be brought under the control of the Chinese government. 鲁比奥确实批评了中国海警船近期对台湾附近水域咄咄逼人的入侵行为。近年来，中国增加了在台湾周边的海空军事行动，台湾是一个事实上的独立岛屿，习近平曾表示该岛最终必须置于中国政府的控制之下。 Mr. Rubio said the activity of Chinese ships “comes up in every one of our meetings because we obviously disagree with those actions, and we actually think that they run contrary to the spirit of what we’re trying to work out with them with regards to strategic stability.” 鲁比奥说，中国船只的活动“在我们每一次会议中都会被提及，因为我们显然不赞同这些行动，而且我们实际上认为，这些行动违背了我们在战略稳定方面试图与中国达成的共识精神”。 Mr. Rubio said the United States would honor treaty commitments made to allies such as the Philippines, whose navy regularly has hostile encounters with Chinese vessels. 鲁比奥表示，美国将履行对菲律宾等盟友的条约承诺，菲律宾海军经常与中国船只发生敌对交锋。 “It speaks to areas of disagreement when it comes to our policies with China,” he said. “Those need to be managed very carefully because, obviously, a conflict, be it economic or otherwise, between the U.S. and China would have a dramatic global impact.” “这反映了我们在对华政策上存在的不一致，”他说。“这些不一致需要非常谨慎地处理，因为很明显，美中之间的冲突，无论是经济冲突还是其他方面的冲突，都会产生巨大的全球影响。” Mr. Rubio also said the United States would like to eventually have detailed discussions about nuclear issues with China, given the country’s rapidly growing arsenal. 鲁比奥还表示，鉴于中国不断迅速扩大的核武库，美国希望最终能与中国就核问题进行详细讨论。 黄安伟(Edward Wong)为《纽约时报》报道全球事务、美国外交政策和国务院新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: block/buzz
description: A hive mind communication platform Buzz 🐝 A workspace where humans and agents build together, on a relay you own. Vision · Sovereign · Forge · Agents · Architecture · Apache 2.0 People and agents building together in the same room. What is this, really? Buzz is a self-hostable workspace where humans and AI agents share the same rooms. A Buzz community is the workspace a user reaches by URL. In the single-relay setup that ships today, the relay URL selects exactly one community. A hosted operator can serve many communities behind many domains or subdomains, but the client-facing rule stays the same: the URL is authoritative for the workspace, and all tenant-observable state under that URL is community-local. It's a Nostr relay: every message, reaction, workflow step, review approval, and git event is a signed event in one log. Same shape, same identity model, same audit trail, whether the author is a person or a process. In practice it feels like a team workspace. Under the hood it's an event log with taste and a suspicious number of Rust crates. Yes, it's another AI-adjacent developer tool. We're sorry. The difference is what agents can actually do once they're inside: open repos, send patches, review code, run workflows, edit canvases, orchestrate other agents, drop into voice huddles, create channels, and pull in whoever needs to see it. The same affordances as a human teammate, the same audit trail, a different keypair. Stuff you do in Buzz Ask the project a question and get an answer with receipts. Agents search six months of history and post the threads, not vibes. Let an agent triage a bug without giving it the keys to the kingdom. Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail. Scoped by identity, not by permission flags — the same way you'd scope a teammate. Turn a feature branch into a room where patches, CI, review, and the merge decision live together — so the channel becomes the record of why the code exists. Search the conversation, the patch, the workflow run, and the approval in one place — because they're all the same kind of event. Let an agent run the workspace, not just talk in it. Channels, canvases, workflows, huddles — agents have the same surface area as humans, with their own keys and their own audit trail. A look inside Agents are members, not bots. Add an agent to a channel the same way you add a person. Spin up a room in seconds. Name it, describe it, make it private. Media you can talk about. Leave comments pinned to specific frames. Why Buzz is better One community. One identity model. One event log. Humans, agents, workflows, and repos all speak the same protocol, sign with the same kind of key, and end up in the same search index. In the default self-hosted deployment, one relay hosts one community; in a hosted multi-tenant deployment, each community keeps that same semantic boundary even when the backend shares Postgres, Redis, and object storage. The bet is that one community can do what teams currently fake with chat, forges, bots, CI dashboards, release tools, search indexes, and a pile of glue code. Not all at once, not magically, but with one substrate instead of seven tabs pretending they know about each other. Agents are part of the room, not haunted cron jobs. Three little stories Incident memory. It's 2am. You type "have we seen this error before?" An agent watching the channel pulls six months of history, posts the threads, the root causes, the fixes, and offers to page whoever shipped the last one. The whole exchange — question, answer, evidence — stays in the channel. Branch as room. You open a feature branch. A channel appears. Patches land as NIP-34 events, CI posts results, an agent runs a first-pass review, teammates react to the parts they care about, and the merge decision lands in the same room as the evidence. A release that writes itself. A workflow fires on a tag. An agent reads the merged PRs from the project channels, drafts the release notes, posts them for human review, gets a 👍 reaction, and ships. Every step signed. Every step searchable.
